summary: the clock suite on x86-64, its one architecture, with each CLOCKLOAD line held two seconds before clockload.py reads it, and the rule that counts one tick for each interrupt

argv: ARCH=x86_64 sh tests/proofs/guest.sh make rach2 test-image && ARCH=x86_64 sh tests/proofs/guest.sh copy ${WORK} rach2/kernel
RACH2_CLOCKLOAD_DELAY_S=2 ARCH=x86_64 exec sh tests/proofs/guest.sh run clock 'clock-test: ok: both clocks kept the host'

faults.name: one-per-interrupt
faults.summary: timer_tick_clock counts one tick for each interrupt once the reference keeps time, so that the host's stops lose the ticks that fell due
